### Independence County

- **Type:** County
- **Status:** 🟢 Active
- **Recorded date:** 2026-08-10 (Independence County Quorum Court unanimous adoption of Ordinance No. 2026-21 at its regular August meeting, reported the next day as a Monday-night vote)
- **Date field:** `2026-08-10` (exact)
- **Duration:** Five-year moratorium on construction of commercial data centers, effective immediately under an emergency clause; runs through Aug. 31, 2031
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center
- **Record ID:** `ar-independence-county-2026`
- **Authority and source:** Ordinance No. 2026-21, adopted with an emergency clause
- **What prompted it:** Preemptive pause adopted with no data center project currently proposed in the county; Justices of the Peace cited the heavy water and electricity consumption of commercial data centers, lack of transparency in land acquisition, and a recent wind-turbine development dispute (a company holding turbine contracts predating the county's 2025 wind moratorium) as reasons to act before any project arrives.
- **Affected projects:** None identified; officials said no data center had been proposed in Independence County at the time of adoption.
- **Status notes:** White River Now reported that the Quorum Court passed a five-year commercial data center moratorium on August 10, 2026, with a reported end date of August 31, 2031 and study of future rules. On August 11, Arkansas Advocate reported a unanimous vote and, citing county officials, no known proposed data center. The legacy record reports an emergency clause and an earlier rulemaking condition; the retained notice excerpt does not establish the operative terms. Recorded active as of September 23, 2026 in the legacy inventory; that historical claim and current legal force are not established by the retained sources. [VERIFY legal force and final ordinance]
- **Outcome:** Preemptive five-year moratorium adopted while the Quorum Court studies commercial data centers and drafts future rules and regulations; the longest data-center moratorium term reported in Arkansas as of this pass.

### HB1444 (2025) -> Act 548

- **Policy ID:** `ar-hb1444-2025-act-548`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. Aaron Pilkington; Sen. Jonathan Dismang; R
- **Status:** Enacted as Act 548, signed 2025-04-10
- **Provisions:** Amended the data center sales and use tax exemption; lowered the qualified data center threshold to $100 million; added a qualified large data center category requiring at least $2 billion of investment over 10 years; included electricity, water systems, storage, cooling, and related infrastructure. For both qualified data center categories, the qualified firm must not be primarily engaged at the facility in adding virtual-currency transactions to a distributed ledger.
- **Mechanism / scope:** incentive_support; fiscal
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://www.arkleg.state.ar.us/Acts/FTPDocument?path=%2FACTS%2F2025R%2FPublic%2F&file=548.pdf&ddBienniumSession=2025%2F2025R>)

### SB78 (2024) -> Act 173 and SB79 (2024) -> Act 174

- **Policy ID:** `ar-sb78-2024-act-173-and-sb79-2024-act-174`
- **Sponsor / party:** SB78: Sens. J. Bryant, Irvin; Rep. McClure. SB79: Sens. Irvin, J. Bryant; Rep. J. Moore; R
- **Status:** Acts 173 and 174 approved and effective 2024-05-03; legislative notifications 2024-05-09
- **Provisions:** In 2024 Act 173 added noise-reduction requirements for covered digital asset mining businesses and barred local ordinances prohibiting or requiring prior approval for home mining. Acts 173 and 174 each amended the earlier local restrictions, removing specified limits on home-mining noise rules, differential business requirements, and discriminatory rezoning while retaining a prohibition on rezoning without compliance with applicable law. Act 174 created state permitting for covered mining businesses with an initial-rules transition and preserved consistent local regulation in areas not otherwise addressed. Both addressed prohibited foreign ownership. Later amendments and current force remain unverified.
- **Mechanism / scope:** permitting_restriction; statewide
- **Legal effect:** unknown
- **Effective date:** 2024-05-03
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://www.arkleg.state.ar.us/Acts/FTPDocument?path=%2FACTS%2F2024F%2FPublic%2F&file=173.pdf&ddBienniumSession=2023%2F2024F>)
